claims.text: HfNbTaTiZr can be produced by powder-metallurgy routes including spark plasma sintering of gas-atomized powder.
Near-pure (<0.12 wt.% oxygen) and oxygen-enriched (1 wt.% oxygen) HfNbTaTiZr states can be prepared with controlled oxygen contents.
A Monte Carlo cluster expansion can capture the temperature-dependent chemical short-range order of HfNbTaTiZr.
Green–Kubo molecular dynamics using on-the-fly machine-learned force fields can calculate lattice thermal conductivity.
The proposed Green–Kubo simulations will determine phonon lifetimes.
The combined cluster-expansion and Green–Kubo approach will be significantly more accurate than perfect-crystal models for HfNbTaTiZr.
Below 200 K, the predicted lattice thermal conductivity will be approximately twice the value predicted by defect-free models.
At high temperature, HfNbTaTiZr containing 1 wt.% oxygen will have a lattice thermal conductivity near 10 W/(K m).
HfNbTaTiZr contains temperature-dependent clusters of chemical short-range order.
Chemical short-range order modifies the vibrational density of states.
Chemical short-range order enhances phonon scattering.
Temperature evolution of short-range order changes local bonding environments and thereby changes phonon lifetimes and scattering rates.
Separate Green–Kubo lattice calculations allow lattice transport to be treated independently of an electronic transport calculation.
Previous analytical and DFT-derived estimates assume perfect, defect-free crystals and omit temperature-dependent chemical short-range order.
Previous estimates often conflate lattice and electronic thermal-transport contributions.
The hypothesis applies to powder-metallurgy HfNbTaTiZr between 100 K and 1200 K.
The hypothesis may fail for HfNbTaTiZr with extremely high oxygen contamination.
The hypothesis may not transfer to other high-entropy-alloy systems with substantially different atomic interactions.
Combining thermal measurements with electronic-contribution subtraction, spectroscopy, and short-range-order characterization can test the predicted lattice conductivity and mechanism.
Failure to observe the approximately twofold low-temperature difference or a high-temperature lattice conductivity near 10 W/(K m) in the 1 wt.% oxygen sample would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis claims improved predictive accuracy, but the quantitative test is framed as a twofold increase in the predicted conductivity rather than a quantified reduction in prediction error against an independent benchmark. A higher predicted value is not itself evidence of greater accuracy.
